newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares index rises 1.6 pct to record high.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares index rises 1.6 pct to record high.

text.p: The Russian Trading System 24-share index rose 1.6 percent to a record 231.48 on Thursday from 227.73 on Wednesday on volume of $39.44 million, data from the NAUFOR brokers association showed.
Dealers said the market had shrugged off worries about President Boris Yeltsin's health after stumbling when the RTS opened on news Yeltsin had gone to hospital with pneumonia.
The RTS-24 index set its previous record of 227.78 on July 4 last year, after Yeltsin's re-election. Its record low was 66.69 on March 18 last year when Yeltsin was trailing in the opinion polls.
On Wednesday turnover on the RTS hit a record $55 million, about twice what is considered a healthy volume.

"We saw some morning panic by locals, but foreigners were much more conservative. They were confident (Yeltsin) was doing all right. Midday prices were attractive. It was immediately picked up," said Troika-Dialog salesman German Zvezdine.

"The Yeltsin news will continue to depress the market. But the times when you could speculate on such news easily are over. Market liquidity is now sufficiently high," said Regent European Securities dealer Dmitry Starenko.
Dealers said there was strong demand from Norilsk Nickel, which had been relatively ignored in the recent rally of leading stocks. It closed at $6.25, up from $5.85.
UES was still in demand in the run-up to publication later this month of the results of the recent auction of 8.5 percent of its shares. It rose to $0.1178 from $0.1097.
Bellwether utility Mosenergo ended at $1.28, down from $1.33 at Wednesday's close, but substantially higher than $1.14 in early trade.
Oil company Surgutneftegaz, which has led the market higher in the recent holiday rally, dropped to $0.575 from $0.600, but was off an early low of $0.535.
Looking ahead dealers said there were signs of a correction in the most liquid shares.
"In principle a normal correction should take place for two or three days from these levels," said Trinfiko dealer Alexander Gritskevich.
"But then the rise will continue, as the market is in the mood for growth. Volumes, the mood of participants, investors views about Russia all point to that," he said.
Starenko said it was premature to talk of a correction.
"It's not yet a correction, just a reduction in demand... It's not yet a correction, just profit-taking in some particular stocks," he said.
